novel_features.name: Odds Value (+EV Finder)
novel_features.description: See which sportsbook's current price beats the vig-free fair line before you bet.
novel_features.rationale: Requires stripping vig from BMR's own free consensus feed to compute a fair probability, then comparing every book's live price against it — a computation no raw API response gives you.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this before placing a bet to confirm you are not just getting the highest number, but a genuinely positive-EV price.

novel_features.name: Steam Move Detector
novel_features.description: Scan today's whole slate for fast, coordinated line moves that signal sharp money before the market fully reacts.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a locally synced consensus-history time series and a rate-of-change computation across the whole board — only possible because the data is cached locally, not from any single live call.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when you want to catch sharp action across an entire day's games rather than watching one event.

novel_features.name: Record a Bet
novel_features.description: Log your own wager (event, market, price, book, timestamp) to a local ledger.
novel_features.rationale: This is the user's own data, not BMR's — no API endpoint could ever provide it; it only exists because the CLI has a local SQLite store.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this immediately after placing a real bet so it can later be graded against the closing line.

novel_features.name: Grade a Bet's Closing Line Value
novel_features.description: Compare one recorded bet's price to the market's closing line to compute its CLV.
novel_features.rationale: Joins the user's local bet record against BMR's historyLines/lineHistory closing data — a cross-source join no single API call provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this after a game closes to see whether you beat the closing number, the standard measure of betting skill.

novel_features.name: Aggregate CLV Report
novel_features.description: See your running closing-line-value percentage and win rate across every recorded bet.
novel_features.rationale: Requires aggregating the local bets ledger accumulated over time — no external API tracks a user's personal betting history.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this weekly/monthly to track betting performance over time instead of grading bets one at a time.

novel_features.name: Arbitrage Scan
novel_features.description: Find risk-free two-sided price mismatches across sportsbooks for one event.
novel_features.rationale: Requires combining the best price on each side of a market from different books and checking their combined implied probability — a cross-book computation, not a single endpoint.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to find guaranteed-profit spreads across books; do not use it to judge single-side value, use odds value for that.

novel_features.name: Line Movement Chart
novel_features.description: See the full open-to-current price timeline for one event and market, across books.
novel_features.rationale: Renders a computed, chronological view from locally synced history — the raw history endpoints return snapshots, not a formatted delta timeline.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to see how a specific line moved over time; use steam scan instead to find movement across the whole day's slate.

narrative.headline: Every sportsbook's price, BMR's own sharp consensus, and full line history — for free, from the terminal, no API key required.
narrative.value_prop: BookmakersReview runs a free, unauthenticated GraphQL feed behind its odds-comparison tool that already includes consensus, opening/current/historical lines, injuries, and weather in one graph. This CLI wraps it, adds a local SQLite history no paid odds API gives you by default, and layers on vig-free value finding, steam detection, and closing-line-value grading that no sportsbook data API — paid or free — ships out of the box.
narrative.auth_narrative: No authentication is required. Every query in this CLI works unauthenticated, exactly like the public odds.bookmakersreview.com tool.

quickstart.comment: confirm the CLI can reach the BMR GraphQL service
find the league id for the sport you care about (NFL=16, NBA=5, MLB=3, NHL=7)
find the best moneyline price across every tracked sportsbook
check whether that best price is actually positive expected value, not just the highest number
scan the whole slate for sharp/steam moves before kickoff

troubleshoots.symptom: A `sports list` style command returns nothing or errors
troubleshoots.fix: the upstream `sports` field is a known broken federation endpoint on BMR's side; use `leagues list` instead, which carries the sport id (`spid`) per league

troubleshoots.symptom: `odds value` / `arb scan` / `odds movement` report no lines/history for a market
troubleshoots.fix: this CLI has no local sync step; every query hits BMR's live GraphQL feed directly. An empty result means BMR hasn't posted lines for that event/market yet (common for games several days out) or the market type doesn't apply to that sport. Confirm data exists first with `odds current --event <id> --market <id> --books <ids>` or `consensus current --event <id> --market <id>`, and try again closer to game time

troubleshoots.symptom: A query returns an empty array with no error
troubleshoots.fix: double-check the numeric id you passed (event/league/market-type ids are BMR-internal integers); use the matching `list` command with `--select` to look the id up by name first

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when you need current or historical sports-betting odds, sharp consensus, line movement, or closing-line-value analysis for U.S.-facing sportsbooks, and want it scriptable/offline instead of manually comparing books in a browser.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to place real bets — it is a read-only odds/data tool with a local bet ledger for your own tracking, not a sportsbook integration.
Do not use this CLI for non-US/offshore-only or niche international leagues without first checking `leagues list` — BMR's coverage is US-sportsbook-centric.
Do not use this CLI as a source of betting advice or guaranteed win probabilities — `odds value`/`arb scan` surface mathematical relationships in published prices, not predictions.

recipes.title: Find the best price across books
recipes.explanation: Returns every tracked sportsbook's current spread price for the event, sorted best-first.

recipes.title: Narrow a large event-history payload to just the fields you need
recipes.explanation: A date-range history query returns every event's full per-period score breakdown; --select keeps agent context small by returning only the id and kickoff time when you just need to enumerate events (follow up with 'events get <eid>' for full scores on the ones you care about).

recipes.title: Check if a price is actually good value, not just the highest number
recipes.explanation: Strips the vig from consensus to compute fair value, then flags any book beating it — the highest number isn't always +EV.

recipes.title: Scan for sharp/steam action across today's slate
recipes.explanation: Flags markets where consensus moved fast and far from the opener across the board, a signal of sharp money.

recipes.title: Track your own closing line value over time
recipes.explanation: Aggregates every bet you've recorded and graded into a running CLV percentage, the standard long-run skill metric for bettors.
